uncertain_or_editorial_candidates.candidate: A one-dimensional plot could show the uniform density on [0,1], the Gaussian kernel centered at x=0 after bandwidth scaling, and the shaded kernel mass over [-1/h,0] tending to 1/2 while the selected target value remains f(0)=1. This would make the boundary truncation responsible for the limiting bias visible; the source already proves the result, so its absence is editorial.
checks: Mark the support interval [0,1] and its boundary x=0.
Show the rescaled Gaussian kernel K(u) and the integration window [-1/h,0].
Label the shaded mass as ∫_{-1/h}^0 K(u)du → 1/2 and the target as f(0)=1.

uncertain_or_editorial_candidates.candidate: For the stated n₁=n₂=2, S=2 case, a three-bar conditional-mass plot could display k=0,1,2 with heights 1/6,4/6,1/6, plus the inclusive upper-tail p-value at each k (1, 5/6, 1/6). The source gives these exact values and explains that larger K favors the one-sided alternative, so the figure is an optional teaching aid rather than a missing-art defect.
checks: Use only the feasible values k=0,1,2 for S=2.
Label bar masses 1/6, 4/6, 1/6, summing to one.
Show inclusive upper tails 1, 5/6, 1/6 and indicate that large K favors the alternative.
